title: Bryan Johnson's 11 daily health essentials: tools he uses to measure and protect his body
summary: Bryan walks through the non-affiliate products he uses daily: stainless steel food storage, certified air quality monitoring, extra virgin olive oil, vagus nerve devices, wearables and body measurements, adjustable dumbbells, red light and scalp care, and a temperature-controlled bed. The through-line is to measure everything, build habits into a morning sequence, and avoid toxins like plastic.

principles.text: Store and eat food in food-grade stainless steel instead of plastic, and use batch-prepped containers to plan meals weekly.
principles.quote: This allows me to plan my meals out on a weekly basis and do so without worried about toxins.

principles.text: Monitor air quality with a certified device and keep doors and windows closed to maintain pristine indoor air.
principles.quote: maintaining pristine air quality in the house requires the proper closing of doors and windows if they're open.

principles.text: Extra virgin olive oil ranks at the top of foods for health; use a lab-tested one, about 15 ml with every meal.
principles.quote: I have extra virgin olive oil with every meal. I do one tablespoon or 15 ml and I pair it with food because it has many health benefits.

principles.text: Shift the nervous system toward calm using vagus nerve stimulation devices and experiment with HRV to find what works for you.
principles.quote: the goal is to get you into chill state more often.

principles.text: Measure constantly with a wearable, daily body temperature and a body-composition scale; the brand matters less than tracking.
principles.quote: Often times people do things but they don't track it to see if it's really working or not.

principles.text: Sleep is the top performance enhancer, and a temperature-controlled mattress meaningfully improves his sleep.
principles.quote: Sleep is the number one performance-enhancing drug of your entire life.
